 Bundesliga Match Report: Bayern Munich outlasts gutty effort from SC Freiburg for 3-1 win
 Take the dub and run back to Bavaria.
 by CSmith1919 Oct 25, 2026, 6:50 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 (Photo by THOMAS KIENZLE / AFP via Getty Images) / DFL REGULATIONS PROHIBIT ANY USE OF PHOTOGRAPHS AS IMAGE SEQUENCES AND/OR QUASI-VIDEO AFP via Getty Images Part Of SC Freiburg vs. Bayern Munich: 2026/27 Bundesliga full coverage see all updates CSmith1919 Chuck Smith is the site manager for Bavarian Football Works, where he began writing in 2017. He is the author of The Daily Schmankerl, the longest-running daily Bayern Munich column in English, and also writes The Weekend Warm-Up. In addition to covering Bayern Munich news and providing commentary on Bayern Munich, the Bundesliga, and the German national team. He brings more than 30 years of sports-writing experience to the site. Over the course of his career, he has written for numerous newspapers and websites. In the end, all that counts is that Bayern Munich found a way to get the job done.
 Despite missing several key players and having Vincent Kompany absent after his collapse earlier this week, Bayern Munich defeated SC Freiburg 3-1 at the Europa-Park Stadion to reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga. Assistant coach Aaron Danks took charge on the touchline, and the visitors delivered an important result ahead of next weekend’s Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund.
 Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring in the 16th minute with a spectacular solo effort. After helping initiate the counterattack, the French defender raced forward, collected a perfectly weighted pass from Michael Olise, and finished calmly past Freiburg goalkeeper Mio Backhaus. It was a striker’s finish from a center-back who continues to demonstrate his value at both ends of the pitch.
 Bayern Munich doubled its advantage just before halftime. Nathaniel Brown delivered an excellent pass into Serge Gnabry, who squeezed his finish past Backhaus in the 42nd minute. The goal was particularly significant for Gnabry, marking his 100th Bundesliga goal.
 The visitors looked comfortable for much of the second half, but Freiburg refused to disappear quietly. Bayern squandered opportunities to put the game away, and the hosts received a lifeline in the 82nd minute when Tom Bischof inadvertently turned the ball into his own net.
 Suddenly, Bayern Munich had a fight on its hands.
 Jonas Urbig stepped up when it mattered, producing a crucial late save to prevent Freiburg from equalizing. Then, in stoppage time, Olise capitalized on a costly Backhaus mistake to seal the 3-1 victory in the 5th minute of added time.
 It was not always pretty, but Bayern Munich showed resilience when the pressure mounted. With Kompany’s health rightfully taking priority, his team delivered three valuable points, reclaimed first place, and set itself up for a massive showdown with Dortmund.
 Sometimes, getting the job done is what matters most.
